binary64_operation_order_contract.accumulation_order: every sum is a scalar left-to-right accumulation over the stated index in strictly increasing order from an explicit initial accumulator; vectorized/pairwise/BLAS reductions are not normative; no fused-multiply-add. The 1/n scaling in the mean and every autocovariance is a SINGLE correctly-rounded binary64 division sum/n, never reciprocal-multiply. The long-run variance is accumulated as omega2=gamma[0] then omega2+=2.0*(w[j]*gamma[j]) for j=1..L in increasing order (per-term doubling, not doubling of the whole sum). The exceedance max over series is a sequential left-to-right max over increasing series index.
binary64_operation_order_contract.comparisons: exact binary64 >=/<= on canonicalized values; no decision tolerance on any tie/exceedance/rejection comparison
binary64_operation_order_contract.fixture_exactness: the Domain 1-3 raw-mean/autocovariance/omega2 unit fixtures use exact-dyadic inputs whose variances are exact squares, so those governed intermediates are order-independent and bit-identical on any conforming platform; the studentized bootstrap fixtures (KAT-STUD-OBS-VS-BOOT-001, KAT-E2E-001) involve an irrational se* and rely on the correctly-rounded IEEE-754 sqrt and division for UNIQUE determination (not on being exact squares); end-to-end p-value/rejection outputs are exact rationals integer/(B+1) once the inputs to the >= comparison are bit-identical. The exact-dyadic micro-fixtures do NOT by themselves discriminate binary64 operation order; registered-dimension (n=2193) determinism is guaranteed by the fully pinned operation order (single division sum/n, per-term-doubled sequential omega2, sequential max) together with correctly-rounded IEEE-754 operations, which is why every implementability row can honestly state additional_choice_required=false for the registered instantiation.
binary64_operation_order_contract.serialization: expected binary64 fixture values serialized as shortest round-tripping decimal (Python repr)
binary64_operation_order_contract.signed_zero: any 0.0 result is canonicalized to +0.0 before comparison, serialization, or denominator classification

integrated_end_to_end_pseudocode: validate: every x[i][t] finite else fail H001_NC_NON_FINITE_INPUT; shape [k,n]
for i in 0..k-1: xbar[i]=hac_mean(x[i]); o2=hac_omega2(x[i],L); se[i]=hac_se(o2,n); t[i]=stud(xbar[i], se[i])
path = build_path(n, payload(dgp,outer,b))   # activated RNG contract; one shared path
for i in 0..k-1: xstar=apply(path, x[i]); num=hac_mean(xstar)-xbar[i]; o2s=hac_omega2(xstar,L); tstar[i]=stud(num, hac_se(o2s,n))
for i in 0..k-1: c_i = #{b: Mstar[b] >= abs(t[i])}; p[i]=(1+c_i)/(B+1); reject[i]=(p[i]<=alpha)

rejected_alternatives.RA-CENTER-GLOBAL-MEAN: center at the pooled/global grand mean; rejected: does not impose the per-series null.
rejected_alternatives.RA-CENTER-NONE: no recentering (uncentered percentile bootstrap); rejected: violates Hall-Wilson guideline 1.
rejected_alternatives.RA-CENTER-PRE-RESAMPLE: pre-center observations (subtract xbar) before resampling; rejected: equivalent for the mean but conflates resample with null transform; we resample raw observations and recenter the statistic (one definition).
rejected_alternatives.RA-HAC-CLAMP-NEGATIVE: clamp negative omega2 to 0; rejected: silently masks a computational defect and alters the studentization denominator; we fail closed instead.
rejected_alternatives.RA-HAC-DEMEAN-AT-NULL: demean residuals by the null value 0 instead of the sample mean; rejected: the HAC SE is a location-invariant nuisance estimate that must demean by xbar.
rejected_alternatives.RA-HAC-DIVISOR-NMINUSJ: sample-autocovariance divisor (n-j) at positive lags; rejected: not the Newey-West 1/T convention and breaks the PSD guarantee (NW1987).
rejected_alternatives.RA-HAC-RECTANGULAR-KERNEL: rectangular/truncated kernel w_j=1; rejected: not PSD, can yield negative omega2 (NW1987, AND1991).
rejected_alternatives.RA-MAXT-NO-PLUS-ONE: p = count/B with no +1; rejected: can produce p=0, an invalid Monte-Carlo p-value (PS2010).
rejected_alternatives.RA-MAXT-QUANTILE-INTERP: quantile/critical-value interpolation for the threshold; rejected: the exact count-based p-value avoids interpolation ambiguity and is equivalent by construction.
rejected_alternatives.RA-MAXT-SIGNED-ONESIDED: signed one-sided max; rejected: the null is two-sided (mean != 0).
rejected_alternatives.RA-MAXT-STRICT-EXCEEDANCE: strict > exceedance operator; rejected: anti-conservative under ties (PS2010); we use non-strict >=.
rejected_alternatives.RA-MAXT-STRICT-REJECT: reject iff p_i < alpha (strict); rejected: we fix equality-at-alpha => reject (non-strict <=).
rejected_alternatives.RA-PATH-CONDITIONAL-ALLOC: allocate the restart-index draw only when a restart fires; rejected: the activated RNG contract allocates the coordinate unconditionally to keep draws position-pure.
rejected_alternatives.RA-PATH-ONE-BASED-NOWRAP: 1-based indexing / truncation instead of wraparound; rejected: Politis-Romano use circular wraparound; RNG contract fixes zero-based mod n.
rejected_alternatives.RA-PATH-PER-SERIES: per-series independent resample paths; rejected: frozen spec requires one synchronous shared path across all nine series.
rejected_alternatives.RA-PATH-REDEFINE-PHILOX: redefine Philox/bounded-integer/coordinate semantics here; forbidden: would contradict the activated RNG candidate; this domain only binds and applies them.
rejected_alternatives.RA-STUD-ABS-INSIDE: take absolute value inside the studentization function; rejected: the sign is retained; absolute value is applied once in Domain 4.
rejected_alternatives.RA-STUD-NON-STUDENTIZED: non-studentized raw-mean bootstrap; rejected: violates Hall-Wilson guideline 2.
rejected_alternatives.RA-STUD-REUSE-OBSERVED-SE: reuse observed se for the bootstrap denominator; rejected: Gotze-Kunsch requires the bootstrap variance recomputed per resample.

selected_conventions.boundary_and_edge_cases: omega2>0 => se=sqrt(omega2/n)>0; omega2==0 (incl -0.0) => se=+0.0; omega2<0 => fail closed H001_NC_NEGATIVE_LONG_RUN_VARIANCE (roundoff-only and materially negative identical; never clamped, because Bartlett is PSD in exact arithmetic so any negative binary64 value is an untrusted computational artifact).
selected_conventions.comparison_operators: omega2 non-negativity test uses exact binary64 comparisons: '<0.0', '==0.0', '>0.0' on the canonicalized (+0.0) value; no tolerance.
selected_conventions.denominators_and_normalization: divisor n (sample length) at lag 0 and at all positive lags, applied as a single correctly-rounded binary64 division sum/n (not reciprocal-multiply); long-run variance weight on lag 0 is 1, on lag j>=1 is 2*w[j] applied per-term (2.0*(w[j]*gamma[j])) and accumulated sequentially into omega2 initialized at gamma[0]; se divides omega2 by n (single division) before the correctly-rounded sqrt.
deterministic_pseudocode: hac_mean(x): acc=0.0; for t in 0..n-1: acc=acc+x[t]; return acc/n
hac_gamma(x,xbar,j): acc=0.0; for t in j..n-1: acc=acc+(x[t]-xbar)*(x[t-j]-xbar); return acc/n
hac_omega2(x,L): xbar=hac_mean(x); o2=hac_gamma(x,xbar,0); for j in 1..L: o2=o2+2.0*((1-j/(L+1))*hac_gamma(x,xbar,j)); return o2
hac_se(o2,n): if o2<0.0: fail H001_NC_NEGATIVE_LONG_RUN_VARIANCE; if o2==0.0: return +0.0; return sqrt(o2/n)
selected_conventions.empty_singleton_degenerate_behavior: n>=1 required; registered n=2193; a zero-length series is outside the governed domain and fails closed H001_NC_NON_FINITE_INPUT before any accumulation.
selected_conventions.indexing_conventions: zero-based t in 0..n-1; lag j in 0..L; autocovariance sum runs t=j..n-1 (n-j terms) divided by n; registered (n,L)=(2193,21) so w[j]=1-j/22.
selected_conventions.non_finite_behavior: any non-finite x[t] => fail closed H001_NC_NON_FINITE_INPUT; any non-finite gamma/omega2/se intermediate => fail closed H001_NC_NON_FINITE_INTERMEDIATE.
selected_conventions.normative_definition: For one series x of length n and lag order L: xbar = (sequential sum_{t=0}^{n-1} x[t] accumulated left-to-right from +0.0) divided by n as a SINGLE correctly-rounded binary64 division sum/n (never reciprocal-multiply 1/n*sum); residual u[t]=x[t]-xbar; sample autocovariance gamma[j] = (sequential sum_{t=j}^{n-1} u[t]*u[t-j] accumulated left-to-right from +0.0) divided by n as a single correctly-rounded division, for j=0..L (divisor n at every lag, centered at xbar); Bartlett weight w[j]=1-j/(L+1) for j=1..L (single division j/(L+1)); long-run variance: initialize omega2 = gamma[0], then for j=1..L in increasing order set omega2 = omega2 + 2.0*(w[j]*gamma[j]) where each w[j]*gamma[j] is rounded, then multiplied by 2.0, then added (PER-TERM doubling and sequential accumulation, NOT doubling of the whole sum); standard error of the mean se = sqrt(omega2/n) with a single division omega2/n then correctly-rounded sqrt. Negative lags are not explicitly represented; symmetry is encoded by the factor 2. Lag 0 is included with weight 1.

selected_conventions.boundary_and_edge_cases: the only object centered is the mean statistic; the observed statistic is centered at the null value 0; the bootstrap HAC se* is location-invariant (it demeans by xbar*) so it is unaffected by this centering.
selected_conventions.comparison_operators: equality/other comparisons not applicable; subtraction only.
selected_conventions.denominators_and_normalization: the centering subtrahend is exactly xbar_i (original observed sample mean); no other normalization.
deterministic_pseudocode: bootstrap_numerator(x_i, path_b): xstar=[x_i[p] for p in path_b]; return hac_mean(xstar) - hac_mean(x_i)
selected_conventions.empty_singleton_degenerate_behavior: n>=1; empty/singleton series outside governed domain (fail closed via Domain 1).
selected_conventions.indexing_conventions: per series i; per bootstrap replication b; xbar*_{i,b} computed on the resampled series x*_{i,b}=x_i[path_b].
selected_conventions.non_finite_behavior: non-finite xbar_i or xbar*_{i,b} => fail closed H001_NC_NON_FINITE_INTERMEDIATE.
selected_conventions.normative_definition: The bootstrap resampled series x*_{i,b} is constructed from raw observations via the shared index path (Domain 5); observations are not pre-centered. The null (mean 0) is imposed on the STATISTIC: observed numerator (series i) = xbar_i - 0 = xbar_i; bootstrap numerator (series i, rep b) = xbar*_{i,b} - xbar_i, where xbar*_{i,b} is the Domain-1 sequential mean of the resampled series. Centering is per series, applied after resampling, once per bootstrap replication, using the fixed original observed mean xbar_i.

selected_conventions.boundary_and_edge_cases: se==0 with zero numerator => 0.0 (no evidence); se==0 with nonzero numerator => fail closed; se>0 => exact binary64 division.
selected_conventions.comparison_operators: se>0.0, se==0.0, num==0.0 tests are exact binary64 comparisons on canonicalized values; no tolerance.
selected_conventions.denominators_and_normalization: observed denominator se_i; bootstrap denominator se*_{i,b} recomputed via Domain 1 on x*_{i,b}; no shared or reused denominator.
deterministic_pseudocode: stud(num, se): if se>0.0: return num/se; if num==0.0: return 0.0; fail H001_NC_ZERO_STANDARD_ERROR
observed_t(x_i): xbar=hac_mean(x_i); o2=hac_omega2(x_i,L); return stud(xbar, hac_se(o2,n))
bootstrap_t(x_i, path_b): xstar=[x_i[p] for p in path_b]; num=hac_mean(xstar)-hac_mean(x_i); o2s=hac_omega2(xstar,L); return stud(num, hac_se(o2s,n))
selected_conventions.empty_singleton_degenerate_behavior: a degenerate bootstrap resample yielding se*=0 is handled by the same stud rule and this is intended by design: se*=0 with zero centered numerator gives 0.0; se*=0 with nonzero centered numerator fails closed H001_NC_ZERO_STANDARD_ERROR (uniquely determined; probability zero for the continuous governed DGPs, and identical to the observed-series rule so both implementers agree).
selected_conventions.indexing_conventions: per series i; bootstrap per replication b; five distinguished objects: observed statistic xbar_i, bootstrap statistic xbar*_{i,b}, null-centered bootstrap statistic xbar*_{i,b}-xbar_i, studentized observed t_i, studentized bootstrap tstar_{i,b}.
selected_conventions.non_finite_behavior: non-finite num or se => fail closed H001_NC_NON_FINITE_INTERMEDIATE.
selected_conventions.normative_definition: One studentization function stud(num, se): if se>0.0 return num/se; if se==0.0 and num==0.0 return 0.0; if se==0.0 and num!=0.0 fail closed H001_NC_ZERO_STANDARD_ERROR. Observed studentized statistic t_i = stud(xbar_i, se_i) with se_i the observed HAC SE. Bootstrap studentized statistic tstar_{i,b} = stud(xbar*_{i,b}-xbar_i, se*_{i,b}) with se*_{i,b} the HAC SE recomputed on the resampled series. The bootstrap denominator is always recomputed; the observed denominator is never reused for the bootstrap. stud returns the signed ratio.

selected_conventions.boundary_and_edge_cases: exact tie (Mstar_b==|t_i|) counts as exceedance (>=); smallest reachable p=1/(B+1); a series with |t_i|=0 has count=B (all Mstar_b>=0) and p=1.
selected_conventions.comparison_operators: exceedance uses non-strict >= ; rejection uses non-strict <= (equality at alpha => reject); all exact binary64 comparisons, no tolerance.
selected_conventions.denominators_and_normalization: p-value denominator is B+1; numerator is 1+exceedance-count; no other normalization.
deterministic_pseudocode: absmax(vec): m=0.0; for i in 0..k-1: a=abs(vec[i]); if a>m: m=a; return m   # abs values, sequential
pvalue(t_abs_i, Mstar): c=0; for b in 0..B-1: if Mstar[b]>=t_abs_i: c=c+1; return (1+c, B+1)
global: exists i with reject_i true
selected_conventions.indexing_conventions: series i in 0..k-1 (registered k=9); bootstrap b in 0..B-1 (registered B=10000); counts range 0..B; p in [1/(B+1),1]; registered alpha=0.05.
selected_conventions.non_finite_behavior: no NaN/inf can reach this stage (invalid se failed closed earlier); if a non-finite |t_i| or Mstar_b appears => fail closed H001_NC_NON_FINITE_INTERMEDIATE (never propagate into max/count).
selected_conventions.normative_definition: Two-sided absolute studentized statistics. Observed max M=max_{i=0..k-1}|t_i|; bootstrap max Mstar_b=max_{i=0..k-1}|tstar_{i,b}| (max over the k series, sequential over increasing i). Adjusted single-step p-value for series i: p_i = (1 + #{b in 0..B-1 : Mstar_b >= |t_i|}) / (B+1); exceedance operator is non-strict >= so an exact tie counts; the +1 in numerator and denominator is the finite-replication correction and the observed statistic participates via that +1. Individual rejection: reject H0_i iff p_i <= alpha (equality at alpha => reject). Familywise (global) rejection event: reject the family iff at least one individual rejection, i.e. min_i p_i <= alpha; because all p_i share one bootstrap max distribution, min_i p_i corresponds to max_i|t_i|=M.

selected_conventions.boundary_and_edge_cases: position 0 has no restart decision; continuation wraps via mod n (index n-1 -> 0); restart draws a fresh uniform index; unevaluated RESTART_INDEX draws consume/shift nothing (each raw word is a pure function of its immutable coordinate).
selected_conventions.comparison_operators: restart comparison is strict integer < (u<p); index wrap is exact integer mod n; LOGICAL_ORDER is the coordinate lattice, physical execution order is never normative.
selected_conventions.denominators_and_normalization: restart probability exactly p/q=1/63 (block length 63); uniform_bounded on 0..n-1 with acceptance limit 2**64-(2**64 mod n), retry cap 8.
deterministic_pseudocode: for t in 1..n-1: if bernoulli_rational(coord(RESTART_DECISION,t),1,63): path.append(uniform_bounded(coord(RESTART_INDEX,t), n)) else: path.append((path[t-1]+1) % n)
apply(path, x_i): return [x_i[path[t]] for t in 0..n-1]   # identical path for every series i
selected_conventions.empty_singleton_degenerate_behavior: n>=1; registered n=2193; no unordered container iteration; no retry/result-dependent draw consumption.
selected_conventions.indexing_conventions: zero-based positions 0..n-1 (registered n=2193); draw purposes INITIAL_INDEX=1, RESTART_DECISION=2, RESTART_INDEX=3 (activated registry); one path shared by all nine series (frozen bootstrap_draw_ordering).
selected_conventions.non_finite_behavior: uniform_bounded retry-cap exhaustion => fail closed H001_RNG_RETRY_CAP_EXHAUSTED (inherited); unknown/duplicate draw purpose => H001_RNG_UNKNOWN_DRAW_PURPOSE (inherited).
selected_conventions.normative_definition: One shared synchronous index path per (dgp_or_case_id, outer, bootstrap) payload, length n, zero-based indices 0..n-1, applied identically to all k series: x*_{i,b}[t]=x_i[path_b[t]]. Path construction is exactly the activated RNG candidate's logical order: path[0]=INITIAL_INDEX=uniform_bounded(coordinate INITIAL_INDEX at sample_position 0, n); for t in 1..n-1, restart=bernoulli_rational(coordinate RESTART_DECISION at sample_position t, 1, 63) (Bernoulli(1/63), strict < on exact integers), if restart then path[t]=uniform_bounded(coordinate RESTART_INDEX at sample_position t, n) else path[t]=(path[t-1]+1) mod n. The RESTART_INDEX coordinate at every t>=1 is logically allocated whether or not the restart fires. This domain restates and binds the activated RNG contract (sha256 e52b1a4733024e4255cf771b97765cff19f7f5e59cf824732784a1abd594812f); it does not redefine Philox, coordinate, bounded-integer, or Bernoulli semantics.

two_independent_derivations.requirement: no shared numerical helper; no import from a production engine; no import from each other; expected outputs independently pinned; both bind the same candidate and fixture set and must agree on every governed fixture output
